headline: Cortisol Spyke Weeks climbs from last to fourth
standfirst: Cortisol Spyke Weeks put up 168.44, the best score of the week and the third-best of the season, and has climbed from last in the power rankings after week one to fourth. Behind the top three, the standings are bunched: six teams sit at 3-2 or 2-3. Adams and Jefferson ran into the week's best score again and is 1-4 despite the fourth-most points in the league. And Team Galakrond is 0-5 after facing 779.6 points, with four of its five opponents posting one of the top two scores in the league that week.
lede_scores: Closest game first. Drake Maye Sucks Ass beat roadrunners by 5.02, the only game this week decided by less than ten, which is what the gold border marks.
lede_rankings: Record carries the most weight now, with recent form, scoring and luck behind it. Where a blurb mentions expected wins, that is a team's record against the whole league each week, scaled to five games: what its scoring has earned, regardless of schedule. The color bar splits this week's points by position.
lede_positions: This week's points by position. michael's backfield put up 68.0 and Ben E.'s receivers 67.8, the two biggest position groups of the week. Over five weeks, Ben E.'s receivers run 23.5 a week above league average, the biggest edge any team has at any position.

labels.lede_season: Five weeks on the board. Ben E. has been first three weeks running. Purdy Seconds to Mars falls four spots, the biggest drop of the week. Cortisol Spyke Weeks climbs three.
labels.cnote: Rank one at the top. Every Monday night adds a column.

takes.2: Five wins, and the only unbeaten team left. Ben E. is 47-8 against the whole league, the best mark in the league, and has now passed michael for the most points scored at 716.5. The floor is the story: every week between 131.1 and 156.6, and wins over michael and CeeDeez Nutz, the second and third-highest scorers. This week's 156.56 was a season high, with Jayden Daniels at 32.3 and Parker Washington adding 30.4 from the flex. The receiver room runs 23.5 a week above average, and Jaxon Smith-Njigba has 139.5 on the season. The backfield is still about five a week below. Expected wins of 4.27 say the 5-0 is mostly earned.
takes.9: Second in points at 709.3, 7.1 behind Ben E., and 45-10 against the field. The only loss came in week three, 146.96 against Ben E.'s 150.84. Jahmyr Gibbs went for 37.7 and leads every starter in the league with 153.7 on the season, and Josh Allen is second at 143.0. Together, quarterback and running back run about 32 a week above average. Receivers and tight end are both below it, and Harold Fannin Jr. gave 1.4 at tight end this week. The bench keeps growing: 369.1 points over five weeks, the most in the league. Expected wins of 4.09 match the 4-1.
takes.8: 4-1 and up to third, with the gentlest schedule in the league. Dake has faced 482.6 points, 58.4 fewer than anyone else. The scoring is mid-table: sixth in points at 596.6, 31-24 against the field, expected wins of 2.82. This week was the steady version, 134.38, with Puka Nacua at 37.7 from the flex and Jordan Love at 25.3. Weekly scores still range from 56.5 to 177.9, the widest spread in the league. Javonte Williams and Ashton Jeanty keep the backfield about eight a week above average. Receivers run about seven below.
takes.4: 168.44, the best score of the week and the third-best of the season, 41.99 above projection. Jaylen Warren ran for 36.8, Isaiah Likely added 32.4, the top tight end score of the week, and George Pickens chipped in 28.0. Last in the power rankings after week one, fourth now. Over five weeks the team sits close to league average at nearly every position, 26-29 against the field, with expected wins of 2.36 next to a 3-2 record. The weekly scores swing: 92.0 and 93.0 in two weeks, 139.4 and 168.4 in two others. Derrick Henry leads the team with 111.8 on the season, and 357.3 points have been left on the bench, second-most in the league.
takes.3: A season low, and a second straight loss. CeeDeez Nutz had scored between 133.2 and 147.3 every week, then posted 117.68 and lost to Team evil by 10.52. Most of the drop traces to two spots: CeeDee Lamb scored 2.9 and Cairo Santos 0.0 at kicker. Jacoby Brissett started at quarterback and gave 25.3, and Christian Watson went for 32.3. Over five weeks this is still the third-highest scoring team at 670.5, 35-20 against the field, with expected wins of 3.18. The two losses came by 0.2 and 10.5. Receivers run 16.9 a week above average. The backfield, 13.0 below, has been the weak spot all season.
takes.11: Drake Maye scored 39.5 for the team named Drake Maye Sucks Ass, the best individual score in the league this week, and it won the closest game of the week by 5.02. That is two straight wins and a 3-2 record. The 124.76 was a season high. Maye has 87.2 on the season, 65.7 of it in the last two weeks. Amon-Ra St. Brown leads the team with 104.2, and Sam LaPorta keeps tight end about four a week above average. The backfield is the gap, about 10 a week below. At 22-33 against the field, expected wins of 2.00 trail the record by a full game.
takes.12: The last two weeks have been season highs: 123.4, then 128.20 to beat CeeDeez Nutz. Scores have gone up in three of the four weeks since week one. Spencer Shrader's 21.0 was the best kicker score of the week, and the Jets defense added 18.0. Joe Burrow (101.2 on the season), Christian McCaffrey (91.3) and Garrett Wilson (86.4) give it depth, and the team is within 3.5 points of average at every position except running back, 6.0 below. kelly has faced 628.8 points, fourth-most, and lost twice by less than three: 0.4 in week two and 2.5 in week four. Expected wins of 2.18 match the 2-3.
takes.5: 131.62 was the fifth-best score of the week, and it ran into the best one. That keeps happening. Adams and Jefferson has faced the week's top score twice and the second-best once, and has seen 712.7 points, second-most in the league. The scoring says this is a winning team: fourth in points at 652.6, 29-26 against the field, expected wins of 2.64. Matthew Stafford gave 27.3, Davante Adams 22.1 and Justin Jefferson 18.8, and only 12.62 points sat on the bench, the fewest in the league this week. Receivers run 11.7 a week above average, third-best in the league, and Kyren Williams leads the team with 109.3 on the season.
takes.7: Down four spots, the biggest drop of the week. 96.0 in week four and 96.56 this week, after a 149.1 in week three. Brock Purdy gave 16.2 and Bijan Robinson 15.8, and the receivers produced 14.9 combined, the lowest at that position this week. That is the season-long problem: receivers run 16.7 a week below average, the worst in the league. The rest of the roster is in good shape. Bijan (121.2) and Purdy (116.6) are the fourth and fifth-highest scoring starters in the league, and Trey McBride gives tight end about seven a week above average. Expected wins of 2.27 next to a 2-3 record say the scoring and the results agree.
takes.10: A second straight season high, 119.74 after 118.1, and a 5.02 loss in the closest game of the week. Malik Nabers went for 29.1, James Cook III 22.8 and Matthew Golden 20.3 from the flex, and the receivers' 60.0 was third-most this week. Since a 61.7 in week two the line has gone up every week: 91.3, 118.1, 119.7. Two spots are holding it back. Tight end runs 7.1 a week below average and defense 4.9 below, both the lowest in the league. At 14-41 against the field, expected wins of 1.27 sit right next to the 1-4.
takes.6: Up one spot on the strength of a 2-3 record, with Team Galakrond dropping below at 0-5. 87.80 was the lowest score of the week for the third week running. Over five weeks Bingo Night is 6-49 against the field, with expected wins of 0.55 next to two actual wins, the biggest gap in the league in that direction. Rhamondre Stevenson (17.5) and Blake Corum (16.2) carried the backfield this week. Deshaun Watson started at quarterback for 12.2, and the tight end spot gave 0.3. Jalen Hurts leads the team with 67.0 on the season.

games.text: The best game of the week. Cortisol is coming off the top score of week 5, Purdy Seconds to Mars off two straight 96s. The projections are almost even, and a Purdy win puts both teams at 3-3.
Closer than the records say. Adams and Jefferson scores like a winning team, and ESPN has this within about five points.
Jahmyr Gibbs isn't in michael's lineup, and roadrunners have set season highs two weeks running. Projected about even.
Dake is the clear favorite. Drake Maye Sucks Ass holds the last playoff spot right now and can't afford to slip.
Galakrond's best shot yet at a first win, projected about 14 points clear. Team evil comes in with two straight season highs.
CeeDeez needs to stop a two-game skid, and CeeDee Lamb has to bounce back from a 2.9.
